title.title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
title.subtitle: Claim: approximating a molecule's electronic ground-state energy is QMA-hard, even with unit-charge nuclei

beats.text: The reduction: any QMA problem becomes a molecule's ground-state energy
Only electrons, clamped nuclei and Coulomb forces: no basis set, field or extra potential
Claim: approximating that energy is QMA-hard under polynomial-time reductions

achievement.label: Hardness of the electronic structure problem
achievement.context: Before: hardness needed a lattice basis or a site-dependent magnetic field (2009)
achievement.note: Worst case only: it says nothing about typical molecules

verify.detail: Both the binary-charge and the unit-charge versions are in Lean
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: both the binary-charge and unit-charge versions

plain: Finding a molecule's lowest energy is as hard as any problem a quantum computer can check, in the worst case

steps: Start from a problem known to be hard even for quantum computers
Encode it in a careful arrangement of atomic nuclei
The molecule's lowest energy now answers the hard problem

voice.text: Only electrons, fixed nuclei and Coulomb forces.
Estimating the lowest energy becomes the problem.
Encode a known hard quantum problem in where nuclei sit; the energy answers it.
Claimed: as hard as quantum verification.
